_comment: Deterministic filters. Edit this file, not the code. Every value here runs before any model call, so tightening these is the cheapest way to improve the digest.
_titles: Merged from her resume (Marketing Program Manager, Vendor Manager) and her own ChatGPT-suggested title list. An earlier draft dropped the bare 'program manager' on the theory that it matched irrelevant Technical/Federal PM postings too — true, but re-checked against a live run and reversed: title matching runs BEFORE the location/salary filters, so an irrelevant onsite match costs nothing in tokens, it's rejected before any model call. Removing it had a real cost with no real saving: it silently dropped two genuinely good GitLab matches ('Senior Program Manager, Enterprise Technology & AI', 'Principal Program Manager, Go-To-Market') whose titles don't contain any of the more specific phrases below, because substring matching is literal and word order varies. Kept broad on purpose now.
_titleExclusions: Caps the search at Senior/current level, per Irtiza's review of the first real digest: 'principal'/'director'/'vp'/'president'/'head of'/'chief' reject a step-above-current-level title (this substring-catches 'SVP'/'EVP'/'AVP' too via 'vp', and 'vice president' via 'president'). This is what removed the two Principal-level GitLab/Snowflake roles from that digest ('Principal Program Manager, Go-To-Market', 'Principal Business Operations Manager, Ops & AI Tooling'). 'Senior' is deliberately NOT excluded — that's her current level.
_salaryFloor: Set to $120,000. A posting that states no salary is NEVER rejected by this — it passes, flagged as unknown, and the scorer is told.
_metros: Per Shivani's direct feedback: onsite/hybrid roles in these three metros are now admitted too, on top of remote roles everywhere (remoteOnly stays true — metros only ADDS to what passes, it doesn't narrow the remote gate).
_locationPriority: Her stated order of preference: Houston, Remote, Dallas, New York. Purely a display-order nudge (see rank.ts) — never excludes a role, never changes its score. A role matching an earlier entry ranks above one matching a later entry, at 2 points per tier step; a real score difference of 3+ points still wins, same balance as unstatedSalaryRankPenalty.
_usRemoteOnly: Set per Irtiza's follow-up: US-remote, not remote-anywhere. Rejects a posting that names a specific non-US country/region with no US option (e.g. 'Remote - India', 'Remote - Netherlands'). A bare 'Remote' with no country stated still passes — never rejected on a guess, same rule as the salary floor.
_experienceYears: Per Shivani's direct feedback: her resume shows 5 years since graduating, and she wants roles asking for 3-6 years — not a step up in required seniority, and not a step down into entry-level. This is an OVERLAP check against a posting's stated range, not an exact match (a posting asking for '3-8 years' still overlaps this band). A posting stating no years requirement at all is never rejected by it — same 'don't guess' rule as the salary floor.
_maxPostingAgeDays: Per Shivani's feedback: surface recently posted roles. A posting with no stated post date is never rejected by this — same 'don't guess' rule as everywhere else. 14 days is a starting point given the twice-daily cadence; tighten or loosen freely.
_unstatedSalaryRankPenalty: Per Irtiza: de-prioritize roles with no stated salary, don't exclude them. Subtracted from a role's DISPLAY-ORDER rank only — never from the score shown, and never from whether it clears scoreCutoff. Weakened from an initial 8 to 3 after a live run flipped Snowflake's GTM & Enablement PM (82, unstated) below Notion's Partner Marketing Manager (78, $235k-260k stated) — a 4-point real quality gap shouldn't lose to a salary-transparency nudge. At 3, a genuine gap of 3+ points still wins on merit; only a near-tie (within ~1-2 points) now favors the pay-transparent role. 0 disables this entirely.
